abstract.p: A conductive fluid leakage sensor capable of detecting a leak from a first electrically conductive or non-conductive container with a conductive liquid disposed therein, has a second or outer electrically conductive coating surrounding a first conducting or non-conducting inner container. Additionally, a non-conducting insulating material may be disposed between the inner container and the outer coating. An electrical connection is made between the inner and outer members and to the conductive fluid disposed within the container, so that conductive fluid leaking from the container that comes into contact with the outer electrically conductive coating creates a pulse, which may be sensed by a sensing apparatus providing an indication thereof.

La présente invention concerne un capteur de fuite de liquide conducteur, apte à détecter une fuite d'un premier contenant électriquement conducteur ou non électriquement conducteur, empli d'un liquide conducteur, et qui présente un second revêtement, extérieur, électriquement conducteur qui entoure un premier contenant intérieur conducteur ou isolant. En outre, un matériau non conducteur isolant peut être placé entre le contenant intérieur et le revêtement extérieur. Une connexion électrique est établie entre les éléments intérieur et extérieur et avec le liquide conducteur déposé dans le contenant, de manière à ce qu'un liquide conducteur, fuyant du contenant, et entrant en contact avec le revêtement extérieur, électriquement conducteur, provoque un signal qui peut être capté à l'aide d'un dispositif capteur, indiquant ainsi la présence d'une fuite.

description.p: FLUID LEAKAGE SENSORS
BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION
1. Field of the Invention

The present invention relates to fluid leakage sensing devices and, more particularly, to a conductive fluid leakage sensing device coupled to an electronic apparatus for indicating the initial occurrence of the conductive fluid leaking from a container.
2. Discussion of the Relevant Art

The prior art contains many liquid leakage systems that provide alarms when a leaking liquid is detected. Typical of these devices is that disclosed in U.S. Patent 2,691,134 issued to C.J. Ford on October 5, 1954, which requires a plurality of sensing devices disposed along the seams of a large reservoir, such as in an airplane gasoline tank. Should the leak occur at one of the seams, the sensor provides an indication that may be read on a meter.

U.S. Patent 4,206,632 issued to Suzuki on June 10, 1980 discloses a liquid leak detecting device that includes two electrical conductors arranged in parallel that is separated from each other by a material comprising a continuously porous polytetrafluoroethyleme (PTFE) that contains an electro-conductive material within its pores . The material disposed between the PTFE changes its resistance when contacted with a leaking liquid.
U.S. Patent 5,203,202 issued to Spencer on April 20, 1993 utilizes a layer of pliable conductive material between a conduit and signal carrying elements disposed along the length of the conduit. The conductive material is a layer of conductive tape wrapped around the conduit . Leakage of the gas from the pressured gas container causes a momentary ballooning of the conductive pliable layer, which upon contact with the exposed portion of the signal carrying elements alters the resistance between the conductors making up the signal carrying elements that is measured directly by the impedance changes.

The present invention overcomes the shortcomings of the prior art by providing a simple fluid leakage sensor and a sensing apparatus that utilizes the initial leakage of the conducting fluid to provide a pulse, which causes an indication on an output device.
SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

A fluid leakage sensor, according to the principles of the present invention, includes an inner member for containing a conductive fluid; a second or outer electrically conductive member, is disposed about the inner member, which may be non-conductive or conductive, and in alternative embodiment may include an electrically non-conductive member, for insulating or reinforcing the inner member, disposed between the electrically conductive outer member and the inner member; connection is made to the electrically conductive outer member and the inner member, which are adapted to be connected across a voltage source. A device for
sensing the electrically conductive fluid leaking from the inner member to ■ the outer member may include a device to provide an audible or visual indication of the fluid leakage.

Therefore, it is a primary object of the present invention to provide a fluid leakage sensor including an inner or first electrically non-conducting or conducting member for containing an electrically conductive fluid; an electrically conductive outer member, disposed about the first or inner member; a connection is affixed to the second electrically conductive or outer member and the inner member, which is connected across a voltage source.

It is another object of the present invention to provide a fluid leakage sensor including a first or inner member for containing an electrically conductive fluid; an electrically conductive outer member, disposed about the first or inner member; an electrically non-conductive member, for insulating or reinforcing the first or inner member, disposed between the electrically conductive outer member and the first or inner member, a connection is affixed to the second electrically conductive or outer member and the inner member, which is connected across a voltage source .

Another object of the present invention is to provide a fluid leakage sensing apparatus, which senses the leakage of a conductive fluid from a member containing the fluid immediately upon its occurrence by sensing a change as the fluid passes between the liquid containing member (inner) and the outer member, providing an
output that activates and audio or visual alarm or any other selective output device such as a fluid flow control.

It is another object of the present invention to provide an apparatus for sensing leakage of a conductive fluid from an inner container immediately upon the initial leakage of the electrically conductive fluid.

The foregoing and other objects and advantages will appear from the description to follow. In the description reference is made to the accompanying drawing, which forms a part hereof, and in which is shown by way of illustration, specific embodiments in which the invention may be practiced. These embodiments will be described in sufficient detail to enable those skilled in the art to practice the invention, and it is to be understood that other embodiments may be utilized and that structural changes may be made without departing from the spirit and scope of the invention. The following detailed description is, therefore, not to be taken in a limiting sense, and the scope of the present invention is best defined by the appended claims. In the accompanying drawing, like reference characters designate the same or similar parts throughout the several views.
BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF THE DRAWING

The subject matter, which I regard as my invention, is particularly pointed out and distinctively claimed in the concluding portion of the specification. My invention, itself, however both to its organization and method of operation, together
with further obvious advantages thereof may be best understood by reference to the following description taken in connection with the following drawing, in which:
FIG. 1 is a greatly enlarged cross-sectional view of one end of the fluid carrying portion of the fluid leakage sensor, according to the principles of the present invention;
FIG. 2 is a partially broken away portion of a hose member utilized to carry a conductive fluid;
FIG. 3 is a greatly enlarged cross-sectional view of an electrically conductive ferrule disposed within the aperture of the fluid containing hose member;
FIG. 4 is a perspective view of the conductive toroid member placed upon the electrically conductive ferrule shown in FIG. 3;
FIG. 5 is a cross-sectional view taken along the line 5-5 of FIG. 4;
FIG. 6 Is a schematic circuit diagram of a sensing apparatus for providing an output indication when the conducting fluid leaks out of the inner container;
FIG. 7 is a greatly enlarged cross-sectional view, similar to FIG. 1, showing one end of an alternative embodiment of the fluid carrying portion of the fluid leakage sensor,
FIG. 8 is a partially broken away portion of a hose member, of the alternative embodiment, utilized to carry a conductive fluid;

FIG. 9 is a perspective view of the conductive toroid member placed upon the electrically conductive ferrule shown FIG. 7 of the alternative embodiment;
FIG. 10 is a cross-sectional view taken along the line 10-10 of FIG. 9.
DESCRIPTION OF THE PREFERRED EMBODIMENT

Referring now to the figures, and in particular to FIG. 1, there is shown an enlarged cross-sectional view of a coupling member 12 disposed on one end of a hose member 13 that is connected on the other end, not shown, to a reservoir in which a conductive fluid is stored, not shown, and which includes the same coupling member 12, that is typically connected in a conventional manner, to a cooperating threaded male connector, not shown. The coupling member 12, includes a threaded portion 14 that is adapted to be affixed to a male threaded portion, not shown, and an S-shaped member 16, shown in cross-section, which receives the other end 18 of the threaded portion 14 of the coupling member 12. The other end 20 of the S-shaped portion 16 is adapted to receive the flared portion 22 of the electrically conductive ferrule 24.

Included within the threaded portion of the connector 14 is a conventional sealing washer 26, which is used to make a sealing connection to the threaded male adapter inserted therein, not shown. The electrically conductive ferrule 24 is adapted to be inserted into the opening 28 provided in the non-conductive hose or inner member 30 or alternatively, into a conductive inner member 30 and is designed to have a force fit when entering the opening 28 of the inner hose member 30.
An electrically non-conductive insulating or reinforcing member 32, may additionally be used, and is preferably of a mesh, spiral or woven construction or alternatively, a member having a plurality of apertures therein, may be used to surround the inner hose member 30 and acts as a reinforcement thereto to give it additional strength, if desired. Surrounding the inner hose member 30 and/or the reinforcing member 32 is an electrically conductive outer hose member 34. The inner hose member 30 and reinforcing member 32 may be fabricated from a non-conductive rubber, nylon or some other type of non-conducting plastic for flexibility. Alternatively, the inner and outer members 30 and 34, may be fabricated from a rubber material, which include a large percentage of carbon black to ensure that it is electrically conductive.

In order to rigidly affix the members 30, (32) and 34 onto the conductive ferrule 24 an electrically conductive clamping ferrule 36 is used to join the members 30, (32) and 34 rigidly to the electrically conductive ferrule member 24, which may include a dimple 38 introduced by a clamping tool, not shown. A perspective view of the hose 13 is shown broken away in FIG. 2. It is important to note that although the electrically conductive ferrules 24 and 36 are mechanically affixed to hose member 13, they are electrically isolated so that there is no electrical continuity between them.

Referring now to FIG. 3, which shows an enlarged view and the detail of the assembly of the conductive ferrule 24 together with toroid member 40 and its connection to the upper and lower output
wires 52 and 54, respectively, which may be included in a two conductor conventional cable 62.

The electrical contacts to the electrically conductive ferrules 24 and 36 are provided by a toroid shaped member 40 shown in perspective in FIG. 4, which has a centrally disposed opening 42, that receives the lower portion 44 of the electrically conductive ferrule 24, as seen in FIG. 3. The toroid 40 has an upper conductive surface 46, a lower conductive surface 48 and an insulated portion 50 disposed therebetween. The upper conductive surface 46 of toroid 40, provides an isolated electrical connection to the electrically conductive ferrule 36, which in turn is connected to the electrically conductive outer hose member 34. The lower conductive surface 48 of toroid 40 provides an isolated electrical connection to the electrically conductive ferrule 24, which in turn provides electrical connection to the electrically conductive fluid disposed inside the inner hose member 30. The construction of the toroid 40 is clearly shown in cross-section in FIG. 5. Before the insulating material 50 is utilized one electrically conductive wire 52 is affixed in a conventional manner (soldering or welding) to the upper surface 46 and a second electrically conductive wire 54 is affixed to the lower surface 48 making electrically conductive contact therewith. The wires 52 and 54 extend beyond the toroid 40 for a desired length, wherein a plug 56 is affixed thereon with one conductive wire 54 being connected to the ring portion 58 and the other wire 52 being affixed to the tip portion 60 of the plug 56. The top or upper portion 46 of the
toroid 40 is maintained as the positive connection while the bottom or lower portion 48 is maintained as the negative connection. Upon leakage of the electrically conductive fluid through the hose wall of the inner hose member 30, the electrically conductive fluid comes into contact (see FIG. 7) or passes through the porous electrically non-conductive insulating or reinforcing member 32, (See FIG. 1) and contacts the inside portion of the outer electrically conductive hose member 34 causing a sudden change that is detected through the related electrical sensing circuitry disclosed in FIG. 6, which will be explained hereinafter, and may further include, a plurality of selected output devices, not shown, to indicate a leakage condition, which may also include a device for stopping the flow of the conducting fluid.

Referring now to FIG. 6, in which is shown a sensing circuit with a receptacle 56' adapted to receive the plug 56 therein with the positive connection being coupled through a high impedance resistor 64 to the positive side of a battery 66, preferably 1.5 volts. The positive side of wire 60 is also coupled directly to the positive side of a high impedance operational amplifier 68 and ground 69, with the negative side of the amplifier 68 being connected to the negative side of the battery voltage 66.

The high impedance differential amplifier 68 isolates the sensor from the circuit common 69, which may or may not be connected to the circuit chassis or earth ground. The capacitor 70 and resistor 72 function as a high pass filter that separates the transients
from the D.C. bias and a y low frequency electrical noise that may pass through differential amplifier 68. The resistors 72 and 74, and amplifier 76 amplify the signal pulse to a level that will set the output toggle circuit 78. The capacitor 80 and the resistor 74 function as a low pass filter that separates the signal pulse from any high frequency electrical noise that may get through the amplifier 68. The toggle 78 is a digital gate that latches out and has a high impedance wnen set and changes to a low value when reset. This serves to maintain an alarm until the reset bottom is se .

In the original design, if we assume that the non-leak resistance is from 10,000 ohms to infinity and a leakage resistance of from zero ohms to 100,000 megohms, then a battery voltage of 1.5 volts and a resistor 64 having a value of 1 megohm will produce a signal pulse of at least -1 millivolts. Although the battery can be an isolated power supply, a small long life battery will probably last for years, since the current drawn from the battery would be in the range of 1.5 microamps, maximum. With the amplifier 68 having a gain of 10 and a voltage supply of 18 volts would raise the bias to 15 volts and the signal pulse to -10 millivolts. These parameters are well within the limits of "off the shelf" differential amplifiers. Selecting the capacitor 70 and the resistance 72 for a time constant of 4 to 5 milliseconds, 4.7 microfarads, and 1,000 ohms that will filter out any 60 cycle noise, which may occur from power lines, as well as, remove the 15 volt D.C. bias from the -10 millivolt signal pulse. To obtain an
inverted gain from the amplifier 76 of 1,000, the resistor 74 should be 1 megohm. This will raise the signal pulse to 10 volts, which is sufficient to set the output toggle 78. Utilizing a .001 microfarad capacitor 80, yields a time constant of 1 millisecond, and with the resistor 74 being 1 megohm, the signal pulse will pass through, but it will block any radio frequency or motor noise.

Referring now to FIG. 7, which is similar to FIG.l, and shows a greatly enlarged cross-sectional view of one end of an alternative embodiment the fluid carrying portion of the fluid leakage sensor, which omits the reinforcing or insulating member 32, with the numerals indicating the same components as set forth in the description of FIG. 1.
FIG. 8 is a partially broken away portion of a hose member 13, of the alternative embodiment, utilized to carry a conductive fluid without the insulating or reinforcing member 32.
FIG. 9 is a perspective view of the modified conductive toroid member placed upon the electrically conductive ferrule 24 shown in FIG. 7 of the alternative embodiment.

Referring now to FIG. 10, which is a cross-sectional view taken along the line 10-10 of FIG. 9 and which clearly shows the change in dimensions to prevent electrical shorting of the conductive hose members (30) and 34 (in alternative embodiment) along member 36 as seen in FIG. 1.

It is to be understood that although the disclosure is directed to specific hose embodiments, it is also suitable for use in detecting leakage from any container or reservoir.
Hereinbefore has been disclosed a liquid leakage sensor and a liquid sensing apparatus, which overcomes the shortcomings known in the prior art . It will be understood that various changes in the details, materials, arrangements of parts and operating conditions, which have been herein described and illustrated in order to explain the nature of the invention may be made, by those skilled in the art, within the principles and scope of the instant invention .

1. A fluid leakage sensor, comprising:
A. an inner member means for containing an electrically conductive fluid;
B. an outer electrically conductive member means, disposed about said inner member means; and
C. coupling means disposed on at least one end of said inner member means and said outer member means .
2. A fluid leakage sensor, according to Claim 1, wherein said inner member means is fabricated from a relatively high resistance material .
3. A fluid leakage sensor according to Claim 1, wherein said outer member means is fabricated from a material having a relatively low electrical resistance.
4. A fluid leakage sensor, according to Claim 1, 2, or 3, wherein said coupling means couples a signal to a sensing apparatus .
5. A fluid leakage sensor, according to Claim 1, 2, 3 or 4 , further including an electrically non-conductive member means disposed between said inner and said outer member means.
6. A fluid leakage sensor, according to Claim 5, wherein said electrically non-conductive member means is fabricated from a material having a plurality of apertures disposed therein.
7. A fluid leakage sensor, according to Claim 5, wherein said electrically non-conductive member means is fabricated from a mesh material .
8. A fluid leakage sensor, according to Claim 5, wherein said electrically ' non-conductive member means is fabricated from a material that is spirally wrapped about said inner member means.
9. A fluid leakage sensor, according to Claim 5, wherein said inner member means is fabricated from a material having a relatively low electrical resistance.
10. A fluid leakage sensor according to Claim 5, wherein said inner and outer member means are fabricated from a material having a relatively low electrical resistance.
11. A fluid leakage sensing apparatus, comprising in combination:
A. an inner member means for containing an electrically conductive fluid;

B. an outer member means, disposed about inner member means ;
C. an electrically non-conductive member means disposed between said inner and said outer member means;
D. coupling .eans disposed on at least one end of said inner member ~:eans and said outer member means and said electrically non-conductive member means;
E. said inner member means and said outer member means being adapted to be connected across a voltage source; and
F. means for sensing said electrically conductive fluid leaking from said inner member means to said outer member means .
12. A fluid leakage sensing apparatus, according to Claim 11, further including output means for providing an indication that the conductive fluid has leaked from said inner member means.
13. A fluid leakage sensing apparatus, according to Claim 11, wherein said output means provides an audible indication.
14. A fluid leakage sensing apparatus, according to Claim 11, wherein said output means provides a visual indication.
15. A fluid leakage sensing apparatus, according to Claim 11, wherein said output means provides a control voltage means for activation of an electrical device.
16. A fluid leakage sensing apparatus, according to Claim 11, wherein said inner member means and said outer member means are connected across a voltage source of approximately 1.5 volts.
17. A fluid leakage sensor, according to Claim 11, wherein said non-conductive member means is fabricated from a material having a plurality of apertures disposed therein.
18. A fluid leakage sensor, according to Claim 11, wherein said electrically non-conductive member means is fabricated from a mesh material .
19. A fluid leakage sensor, according to Claim 11, wherein said electrically non-conductive member means is fabricated from a material that is spirally wrapped about said inner member means .
20. A fluid leakage sensing apparatus, comprising in combination:
A. an inner member means for carrying a fluid having an electrically conductive ferrule disposed therein;

C. said electrically conductive clamping ferrule means and said electrically conducting ferrule means being adapted to be connected across a voltage source; and
D. electrical circuit means for sensing said electrically conductive fluid leaking from said inner member means to said outer member means.
